system_description.narrative_title: Chokepoints, Wars and Tech Rivalry: a Multipolar Order in Flux
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system where regional wars, energy and shipping chokepoints, and high-tech competition generate rapid feedbacks across markets, alliances and domestic politics. Conflicts in Europe and the Middle East, reinforced by coercive economic tools and tariff diplomacy, are compressing supply chains and elevating the strategic value of cyber, space and Arctic routes. States and large firms respond with hybrid measures—naval deployments, trade barriers, alternative shipping corridors and AI-enabled operations—producing volatile cross-border cascades rather than stable equilibria.
system_description.scope: States, alliances and coalitions; transnational corporations and supply chains; energy and commodity flows; global shipping routes and chokepoints; financial and commodities markets; cyber and AI contestation; military deployments and proxy conflicts; international institutions and informal blocs.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-economic-political system (global human governance and economy within the Anthropocene)

variables.name: Strait of Hormuz confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran are locked in a naval and economic struggle over control and access through the Strait of Hormuz, shifting toward sustained maritime pressure, attacks on shipping and US threats of indefinite blockades that threaten global oil flows.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and Black Sea contest
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain in a sustained high-intensity conflict that increasingly targets ports, refineries and grain corridors in the Black Sea, altering maritime security, trade flows and export chokepoints.

variables.name: US–China strategic rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are intensifying competition across trade, technology, supply chains, Arctic and maritime influence and cyber operations, driving decoupling, export controls and new spheres of economic and strategic competition.

variables.name: Israel–Palestinian–Lebanon escalation
variables.description: Israel’s military operations, settler violence in the West Bank and strikes across southern Lebanon involving Hezbollah are producing cross‑border escalation and humanitarian strain, shifting the Israeli–Palestinian front toward wider regional spillover risks.

variables.name: Allied rearmament and defence-industrial shift
variables.description: NATO members, the United States, Japan and partners are rapidly reconfiguring procurement, shipbuilding and missile production to replenish stocks and secure defence supply chains, shifting the global defence industrial base and burden‑sharing dynamics.
